overclaims.page: privacy.html:223 and the whole THE APP section
overclaims.text: Everything below happens at app.field-lux.com, after you create an account (and no telemetry clause at all)
overclaims.reality: The deployed build (rebuild 20a60290, event beacon on) writes app_open with authenticated=false and share_view anonymous=true to fieldlux_app_events with a persistent visitor id, session id, peppered IP hash, user agent, referrer, path, screen, locale, timezone and utm fields; retention 180 days; the only opt-out is an undocumented localStorage key.
overclaims.fix: The app keeps a first-party usage record: one visit row per browser session and a short list of named events such as opening the editor, adding a projector or exporting a PDF. Each row holds a random visitor id kept in your browser, a hash of your network address rather than the address, your browser and screen type, language, time zone, the page path, the referrer and any campaign tags in the link, and your user id if you are signed in. Rows are pruned after 180 days. No third-party analytics script is loaded.

overclaims.reality: The daily job (03:45 UTC) deletes signup-verification rows older than 30 days; each row lives about 30 days. Founder claim request logs have no prune cron.
overclaims.fix: Signup verification logs are kept for 30 days and then removed by a daily cleanup job.

overclaims.text: Each attempt to resolve a link writes one row holding the link's id, the outcome, and a hash of the requesting network address rather than the address.
overclaims.reality: Rate-limited attempts write no row; the hash pepper is a constant committed to the repo, so IPv4 hashes are brute-forceable.
overclaims.fix: Each attempt to resolve a link, other than one turned away by the rate limiter, writes one row holding the link's id, the outcome, and a keyed hash of the requesting network address rather than the address itself.

overclaims.text: One route and one address. ... Email jay@field-lux.com ... and say which of the three you want.
overclaims.reality: Deletion has two routes: the in-app Account settings 'Schedule deletion' control (7-day grace) plus email. Correction and export are email-only.
overclaims.fix: One address. The account email is what proves the request is yours, so it is the only thing we ask you for. You can delete your account yourself from Account settings in the app, or email us for deletion, correction or export.

overclaims.text: Your email address is your FieldLux ID, and it is the only value that tells one account from another.
overclaims.reality: Signup also requires a self-declared role stored in auth metadata (fieldlux_role) and fieldlux_member_profiles.role, and the consent row stores the browser user agent; neither is mentioned.
overclaims.fix: Your email address is your FieldLux ID. Signing up also asks for your role (for example Technical Director or Lighting Designer), which is stored with your account profile along with the consent record and your browser's user agent string.

overclaims.text: Last updated: September 6, 2026 / The date under the title moves when the text does.
overclaims.reality: Site behaviour changed 2026-09-07 (embedSrc removed, fieldlux_pricing_period added) without the date or the clauses moving.
overclaims.fix: Update clauses 02 and 03 as above and set the date to the day of that edit.

overclaims.fix: width="1363" height="805"

overclaims.text: Card index 'FLX' / Project file
overclaims.reality: The real extension is .flx.json (File menu hint); no bare .flx file exists.
overclaims.fix: Project file (.flx.json): move an editable FieldLux plan between accounts or machines.

overclaims.text: Enable motion
overclaims.reality: The script writes data-motion 'full' but the CSS opt-back-in value is 'on' and the .v3-page reduced-motion floor has no escape, so for OS-reduced-motion visitors only the canvas resumes; privacy/404 write 'on'/'off' to the same key, so a choice on /privacy forces full motion on the v3 pages.
overclaims.fix: Either rename the button 'Enable light field' or have every page write and read the same fieldlux_motion values and add html[data-motion=on] to the .v3-page reduced-motion exception.

underclaims.text: Import a 3D model or floor plan, then work at real scale. / Import a 3D model or floor plan, draw the room
underclaims.reality: Prod imports OBJ, FBX, GLB, glTF, DAE, STL and PLY with automatic unit detection and a Y-up/Z-up fix; floor plans load as DWG/DXF linework or as PDF/PNG/JPG placed at a typed physical size; 'draw the room' is a full sketch lane (New Sketch, snapping, Raise walls with W, Make face, Flip Normals) whose walls block light and cast shadows.
underclaims.fix: Import a 3D model (OBJ, FBX, GLB, glTF, STL) or a DWG, DXF or PDF floor plan, or sketch the room from scratch and raise its walls. Everything sits at real scale.

underclaims.text: Choose an Epson, Panasonic or Christie head and a lens from its compatible list, or add a custom head.
underclaims.reality: For Epson and Panasonic heads the Center Illuminance readout is cross-checked against the manufacturer's own calculator (Panasonic TDC, Epson PTDS, 642 combos); custom heads are saved to a reusable list with 11 lens profiles; out-of-spec UST placements are flagged with a diagnostic block.
underclaims.fix: Choose an Epson, Panasonic or Christie head and a lens from its compatible list. Epson and Panasonic lux readouts are cross-checked against the manufacturers' own calculators. Add and save custom heads from any spec sheet.

underclaims.text: Set throw ratio and lens shift, then build linear, circular, or mirrored arrays.
underclaims.reality: Arrays can stay live (move the source and every clone follows), export a coordinate table, and heads can be aligned to one another with the match axes dock; per-axis position locks exist.
underclaims.fix: Set throw ratio and lens shift, then build linear, circular or symmetry arrays that stay live as you move the source, with a coordinate table for the rigging call.

underclaims.text: Use the Mapping Stage to place images or video on a surface and preview playback in 3D. / correction and blend preview / Play Dock preview
underclaims.reality: Play Dock ships Output Setup (regions from beams), a Warp & Blend Studio with corner-pin, mesh warp, masks, per-head soft edge and calibration patterns, a Media Library with uploads, playlists and loop modes, and per-edge auto-blend detection in the Inspector.
underclaims.fix: Map images or video onto the surface, corner-pin or mesh-warp each head, set the soft edges and preview playback in 3D. Play Dock previews the show; it does not control or output it.

underclaims.text: every overlap in view / keep the optics tied to the rig
underclaims.reality: Overlap is not just visible: the Inspector's Edge Blending section detects seams, sets per-edge overlap in percent and metres, and blend groups are created automatically for baked arrays.
underclaims.fix: Every overlap in view, with the seam width and feather set per edge.

underclaims.text: Turn the current setup into a readable technical handoff. / PDF export
underclaims.reality: The Tech Rider PDF carries a viewport image with lux legend, a project setup table (projectors, total lumens, target), a projector index and a per-projector detail page, headed by a 'not a field measurement' disclaimer band. It is one click from the File menu and also available from the share viewer.
underclaims.fix: One click exports a PDF Tech Rider: scene view with legend, projector index, and a page per projector with lens, throw, position and lux.

underclaims.text: Create a review link, then revoke it when the review is over. / read-only link
underclaims.reality: Cloud Share links include the 3D models, show a QR code, can carry a password (stored hashed) and an expiry you can extend, and are listed in Share Management; a colleague with a FieldLux account can be given read-only project access by email; the viewer can toggle the heatmap and export the Tech Rider.
underclaims.fix: Create a read-only link with a QR code, optional password and expiry, extend or revoke it later, or grant a colleague's FieldLux account read-only access by email.

underclaims.text: Read estimated illuminance in lx, combining every projector that reaches the sampled point.
underclaims.reality: The legend can switch between the Composite and each projector's own distribution, a hover probe gives lux and mm/px under the cursor, and Lens View frames the surface from the projector's optical axis; the Measurement target picker lets you choose any room wall including the ceiling.
underclaims.fix: Read illuminance in lx at 13 probes or under the cursor, for all projectors combined or one head at a time, on any wall you choose.

underclaims.reality: Materials are editable: presets, reflectance in percent and screen gain, and the luminance ramp scales with reflectance x gain / pi.
underclaims.fix: including the surface material you set, with editable reflectance and screen gain.

underclaims.reality: The ambient light preset plus lux field yields a projection-to-ambient contrast ratio chip (CR n:1) with a viability verdict from Optimal (Full Blackout) to Not viable; that is a real, deployed answer to 'will it read under house lights' and the site never states it.
underclaims.fix: Set the ambient light of the venue and read the projection-to-ambient contrast ratio beside the heatmap.

underclaims.text: LUX HEATMAP shows the Physics Model
underclaims.reality: The accuracy chip has three states, Physics Model, Spec-based and Calibrated, so the basis is labelled even when a manufacturer calculator figure is in use.
underclaims.fix: The Heatmap panel labels the basis of the number: Physics Model, Spec-based, or Calibrated.

underclaims.text: Fixture photometry and Isolux Working Plane / Fixture schedules and Play Dock preview
underclaims.reality: The lighting lane also imports GDTF and MVR fixture files and IES/LDT photometry, projects gobos, saves Looks (cues), and exports the fixture schedule as CSV; it is the only mention of lighting on the entire site.
underclaims.fix: Fixtures from GDTF, MVR, IES or LDT files, Working Plane (Isolux), looks, and a fixture schedule export.

underclaims.text: Check any point on the surface. / check the value at any point
underclaims.reality: The probe reads Surface lux and pixel pitch in mm/px, live as the cursor moves.
underclaims.fix: Read lux and mm/px at any point on the surface as you move the cursor.

underclaims.reality: Account deletion is self-serve in Account settings with a 7-day cancellable grace period; the page hides a control that already exists.
underclaims.fix: Delete your account yourself from Account settings in the app, or email jay@field-lux.com from the address on your account for deletion, correction or export.

underclaims.text: shared workspaces and seat management are not available yet / No card required
underclaims.reality: Not wrong, but the page never says that saved projects are cloud-stored, autosaved on an interval you set, and version-historied with Restore, which is the reassurance a paying buyer wants before the plan-expiry FAQ.
underclaims.fix: Projects are saved to your account, autosaved on an interval you choose, and every save is kept in version history.

crossPageInconsistencies: Beta-availability wording differs on every page and all versions overclaim: index.html:205 'All features are available today.', product.html:183 'EVERY FEATURE IS OPEN TODAY.', pricing.html:52 'Every feature is available today.', pricing.html:162 'every current feature', videos.html:95 'Every current feature is available during beta.', videos.html:94 'full product', pricing.html:184 'full product'. The app itself shows 'Temporarily disabled in the open beta.' on the Report Builder row.

Heatmap feature name: index.html:103,107 'Lux Heatmap' (hero, locked); measurement.html:81,116,189 'LUX HEATMAP'; the embed button reads 'LUX HEATMAP'; the deployed app says 'Heatmap Overlay' (View menu) and 'Heatmap' (panel). No page uses the app's label.

13-point probe name: measurement.html:151 kicker '13PT DIAGNOSTIC', measurement.html:81 and 404.html:145 '13-point Diagnostic', measurement.html:8 and videos.html:85 '13-point distribution'; the app's only label is '13pt Diagnostic'.
Third placement mode: index.html:144 'mirrored placements', product.html:123 'mirrored arrays', app 'Symmetry'.

Play Dock tier: pricing.html puts 'correction and blend preview' under Projection (:93) and 'Play Dock preview' under Pro (:110,:117), but warp/correction and group blend live inside Play Dock in the app, so the Core tier is promised a preview that the Pro tier owns.
Pro 'Most complete' chip (pricing.html:108) versus Enterprise 'Everything in Pro' (:137): Enterprise is the most complete plan by the page's own definition.
Enterprise weekly cell 'Monthly only' (pricing.html:123) versus its billing line 'CHOOSE MONTHLY OR YEARLY' and a defined yearly price ($82/mo, :125).

Hedging of billing notes: yearly note 'The lowest planned rate' is hedged, weekly 'A seven-day pass. One payment, no renewal.' and monthly 'Billed monthly. Cancel before the next billing date.' (site-experience.js:106-108, pricing.html:71) read as live terms while every card says 'Planned after beta'.

Projector count in the home page: hero copy says 'Eight projectors' and readout '8' (index.html:82,92), while the screenshot two sections below (hero-stitch-01.png at index.html:166) shows a 4-projector scene; product.html:81 captions the same image 'Four projectors'.

Workflow stage vocabulary: index.html ticker 'PLAN THE VENUE / CHOOSE THE OPTICS / READ THE SURFACE / HAND OFF THE PLAN'; product.html cards 'SIMULATION / PROJECTOR LIBRARY / PLACEMENT TOOL / PLAY DOCK / DELIVERABLES'; videos.html 'venue, projection, measurement and handoff'; pricing.html 'placement, coverage, measurement, and handoff'; the app's workspaces are 'Design' and 'Simulate' and its menus Modeling / Projector / Lighting / Share. product.html:109 labels the venue-building card '01 / SIMULATION' while the app calls that the Design workspace and 'Simulate' is the projector stage.

Home meta description (index.html:7) promises 'content mapping'; product.html and every other page say 'content preview'; og:description on index.html:11 says 'a 3D plan your team can review' (a third message for the same page).
PDF naming: index.html:182, product.html:135, videos.html:86 say 'PDF Tech Rider'; pricing.html:171 FAQ says only 'PDF export' (which a reader may take to mean the Report Builder, prod OFF).

Nav and title conventions: header nav says 'Videos' on all pages while 404.html:210 footer says 'Feature videos' and 404.html:151 aria-label 'Feature videos'; index.html title is 'FieldLux | Plan projection before load-in' while every other page is '<Page> | FieldLux'.
Copyright line: v3 pages '© 2026 FieldLux. Open beta.' versus 404.html:219 'Copyright 2026 FieldLux. Open beta' (no symbol, no period); privacy.html footer matches the 404 form.

Favicon declaration: index, pricing and videos link /favicon.ico; product, measurement, privacy and 404 link /assets/favicon-32.png and favicon-16.png plus apple-touch-icon; only some pages carry og:image:alt.

Storage disclosure: privacy.html:175 lists four localStorage keys and says 'Those four are everything'; the site actually writes fieldlux_motion, fieldlux_pricing_period, fieldlux_flow_app_url, fieldlux_discord_url (and never fieldlux_embed_src). Motion key values also disagree between page families ('reduced'/'full' on v3 pages, 'on'/'off' on privacy and 404).

Site-versus-app analytics: privacy.html:172 'no analytics' is true for the static pages but the app the CTAs lead to runs Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights, Google Fonts and a first-party event beacon; the privacy page's app section is silent on all four.

Lighting lane visibility: pricing.html sells fixtures, isolux and fog as Pro features (:106-116) while index.html, product.html, measurement.html and videos.html never mention lighting, so a reader arriving at pricing meets a product lane the rest of the site did not introduce.
Catalog spelling: product.html:117,145 and 404.html use British 'catalogue'; the app UI uses 'catalog' (ProjectorTab 'catalog datum', Projector Library).
Discord tooltip on 404.html:45 says the community grants 'beta access'; product.html:165 uses Discord for spec-sheet submissions; pricing and privacy say signup is public with no waitlist.
